The woman found shot near her Vero Beach-area home Sunday has been identified as 52-year-old Dawn Kriskewic, the Indian River County Sheriff's Office confirmed Tuesday. Investigators delayed releasing her name while they worked to locate and notify several out-of-state next of kin. Kriskewic was found in the 500 block of First Street , just outside Vero Beach, Sunday morning. Deputies performed lifesaving measures before she was taken to a trauma center, where she later died. See also: 17-year-old Boynton Beach teen arrested in deadly park shooting of 19-year-old Investigators have identified 33-year-old Matthew Waggle as a person of interest in the homicide. He has yet to be located or charged. A nationwide BOLO has been issued for Waggle. Investigators say he should be considered armed and dangerous and should not be approached. The Sheriff's Office previously said investigators believe Kriskewic had been trying to end a relationship with Waggle and are investigating the shooting as a domestic violence homicide. The agency has also been using its Real Time Crime Center and a network of Flock license plate cameras as investigators search for Waggle and work to piece together what happened. The investigation remains ongoing. The Sheriff's Office said there are no further updates ready for release at this time.

Suspended Palm Beach County Clerk of Court Michael Caruso made first appearance at the Palm Beach County Criminal Justice Complex Wednesday morning. Caruso was arrested Tuesday morning and immediately suspended from office by Gov. Ron DeSantis on five felony child sex abuse charges.According to the arrest warrant and affidavit filed in Orange County Circuit Court, Caruso, 67, faces charges of kidnapping, lewd or lascivious molestation, lewd or lascivious exhibition, luring or enticing a child and child abuse causing mental injury.In court on Wednesday, the judge ordered set a recheck date for Sept. 2, giving Orange County officials two weeks to pick up Caruso for transport.At the state's request, the judge issued a comprehensive no-contact order that was served to Caruso in court. The order prohibits any contact with the alleged victim, immediate family, witnesses and any individual under the age of 18. The judge emphasized the scope of the order, asking Caruso directly if he understood the restrictions, to which he responded "Yes, sir."When Caruso's defense attorney requested consideration for an extradition bond that would allow him to stay out of jail while waiting to be transported, and the judge firmly denied the request, stating it was inappropriate "based upon the nature and extent of these particular charges."Caruso's attorney, Jason Weiss, gave WPTV this statement following the court event: "Mr. Caruso is innocent of these allegations and intends to vigorously defend himself against these charges.We look forward to his expeditious transfer to Orange County so that appropriate bond conditions can be set."The judge clarified that the Palm Beach County court was not making any probable cause findings, but was only facilitating Caruso's expedited transfer to Orange County where the charges originated.According to court documents, the charges stem from allegations involving multiple incidents with a child victim spanning nearly a year, including incidents during a family cruise in August 2025.The victim disclosed the abuse during a recorded interview with Orange County law enforcement and has been receiving therapeutic services since April 2026. When confronted by family members in December 2025, court documents state Caruso made partial admissions while making threatening statements about potential consequences if the allegations were reported.Shannon Ramsey-Chessman, the chief of staff and chief deputy clerk, has been appointed as interim clerk following Caruso's suspension. The Florida Department of Law Enforcement is overseeing the transition and ensuring no files or records are removed from the clerk's office.Caruso will remain in custody until his transport to Orange County, where he will face the charges.Questions remain about Caruso's status on the November ballot, where he was scheduled to face Democrat Yvette Drucker for the clerk position. The Palm Beach County Supervisor of Elections is awaiting guidance from state officials on how to proceed with his candidacy.The investigation remains ongoing, and additional details will be provided when available.

When an active-duty Army soldier's pet underwent surgery on the wrong shoulder, a North Palm Beach veterans organization stepped in to provide financial support during a difficult time.WPTV anchor Mike Trim recently spoke with the Wounded Veterans Relief Fund about their decision to help the serviceman and his girlfriend, who had already exhausted their savings paying for the initial procedure. The couple had even sold their motorcycle to cover the original surgery costs, leaving them with limited resources to address the veterinary error."Every single day we're helping veterans that come to us with emergency needs," explained Mike Durkee, executive director of the Wounded Veterans Relief Fund, during an interview at the organization's North Palm Beach office.WATCH: When board member and attorney Willard Shepard brought the situation to Durkee's attention, the response was immediate."Hearing the desperation from the service member who just spent all the money to get the operation done and not have additional funds," Durkee said, describing what motivated the organization's quick action.The Wounded Veterans Relief Fund covered more than $1,000 in veterinary bills. We all love animals, right? Especially our combat service members," Durkee told Trim.The Cane Corso dog is now recovering well following the second surgery."We felt really grateful. You know, extremely appreciative that they reached out and were able to help us with funds here and there," co-owner Raphie Shin said. Meanwhile, Shepard is representing the couple as their attorney to address the circumstances surrounding the first surgery. The veterinarians involved in the original procedure declined to comment when contacted.

A Miami woman was arrested in Martin County after allegedly posing as a bank representative to scam residents out of thousands of dollars, according to Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek. Newly released aerial footage shows sheriff's deputies following the suspect, 32-year-old Monquie Turnbull, on I-95 before stopping her vehicle. Body camera footage captured Turnbull exiting her car and being questioned by deputies. "You’re going to be placed under arrest," a deputy said in the footage. Budensiek said Turnbull drove from Miami to Martin County, where she approached two residents, claiming their debit cards were compromised and needed to be turned in for replacement. "They stated that their card was compromised and they needed to turn their card in and they were going to replace their card for them," Budensiek said. One resident was scammed out of hundreds of dollars. "The victim notices pretty quick that not long after the suspect left, there’s $3,180 now missing from her account," Budensiek said. While investigators were handling that case, they received a second 911 call matching the suspect’s description and vehicle. Deputies began their search. Deep Dive: WPBF 25 News Investigates "She was located as she came eastbound on Bridge Road and then she turned around and was going westbound on Bridge Road, which is the video you saw her getting arrested," Budensiek said. Officials later discovered Turnbull had entered the jail with about $3,200 hidden in one of her body parts. "She took our first victim’s card, withdrew $3,180, and that’s the exact amount recovered from inside her person in the jail," Budensiek said. The sheriff urged residents to be cautious if someone comes to their home claiming to be from a bank and asking for credit cards. "This particular incidence, this was all the money that this lady had, this was her rent money, it was everything that she had, and she handed it over to a scammer," Budensiek said. The sheriff is asking anyone who may have been a victim to contact authorities. Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25

The Miami woman accused of posing as a bank representative to scam a Martin County senior is now facing an additional charge after deputies say she tried to smuggle thousands of dollars in cash into jail hidden in an unexpected hiding spot her lady parts. According to the Martin County Sheriff's Office, Monquie Love Turnbull never mentioned she was carrying $3,180 in cash concealed in her body when she was arrested, and the money wasn't discovered until she was being processed into the jail. The sheriff's office has since confirmed the cash is the same money taken from one of her alleged scam victims. Sheriff John Budensiek said Turnbull revealed she had the money inside her body when she complained of pain during a jail phone call to an unknown man. "Our detectives went back over to the jail. They interviewed her yet again. She admitted to having money inside of her. She said at that point it was only $400. And then later, as they interviewed her a little more, she said it was $3,180," said Budensiek. According to the Martin County Sheriff's Office , the case began Monday when 31-year-old Monquie Love Turnbull showed up at an elderly victim's home claiming the person's bank account had been compromised. She told the victim she was with the bank and offered to take the debit or credit card off their hands to dispose of it safely. The victim grew suspicious of the encounter and contacted law enforcement, giving deputies time to track Turnbull down before she left the county. Arrest affidavits show the scheme was more coordinated than initially known. Investigators say an unidentified male caller, posing as a Chase Bank fraud representative, told the victim her account had been compromised and that someone would come to her home to collect and destroy her card before a replacement arrived. Turnbull, using the alias "Monica," then arrived at the home, verified herself with a code relayed from the caller, and collected the card, cutting it in half in front of the victim and placing the pieces in a manila envelope. The victim told deputies she grew uneasy and wrote down Turnbull's license plate number as she left. Minutes later, the victim's bank account was drained through a $3,000 withdrawal and a $180 ATM withdrawal, a total of $3,180. "In this particular instance, this was all the money that this lady had. This was everything that she had. And she handed it over to a scammer," said Budensiek. While deputies were investigating that report, the sheriff's office says they were alerted to a second call identifying Turnbull as a possible suspect in a nearly identical incident targeting another victim the same day. That attempt was caught on a Ring doorbell camera, but the second victim's family member grew skeptical and refused to hand over the card. That victim also provided a plate number and vehicle description, which helped investigators track Turnbull down. Deputies located the vehicle, a gray two-door Nissan Altima, on Bridge Road in Hobe Sound near the I-95 interchange and conducted a traffic stop. Body camera footage shows deputies pulling her over during the stop and placing her under arrest, with the arresting deputy telling her she was being taken into custody for a scheme to defraud. The first victim was brought to the scene and positively identified Turnbull as "Monica" from about 15 feet away. A search of the vehicle turned up a surgical mask and multiple yellow envelopes matching witness descriptions. Turnbull was booked on charges including scheme to defraud, grand theft, fraudulent use of a credit or debit card without consent involving a victim 60 or older, fraudulent use of ID without consent, and felony use of a two-way communication device to facilitate a felony. Investigators say her cellphone and Apple Watch were seized, and a search warrant for the devices is pending. The Sheriff says there are still missing details in this investigation. She stated that she is part of a larger organization. We can't verify that one way or the other, and then the other question we have is: How does she know where to go? She went to two Chase Bank customers. Just random addresses, but it doesn't look to be that random," Budensiek said. See also: Suspended PBC clerk Mike Caruso makes first appearance on child sex abuse charges Turnbull now faces a charge of introducing contraband into a corrections facility on top of her original charges. She's being held on a $500,000 bond. The investigation remains open, including efforts to identify the second suspect who made the phone calls. The Martin County Sheriff's Office is renewing its warning to residents, especially seniors, not to let anyone into their home who wasn't scheduled to be there, and never to hand over cash, credit cards or valuables to someone who shows up unannounced. Anyone approached by someone claiming to represent a bank, financial institution or other organization asking for valuables or access to their home is urged not to comply and to call 911 instead.

A 23-year-old Fort Pierce man was arrested Sunday after deputies say he fired through a locked door with a woman on the other side and fled. Lucie County Sheriff's Office said deputies responded around 11:30 a.m. 16 to a home in the 1700 block of Wyoming Avenue for a domestic disturbance. Investigators said Nathan Hsu was involved in an argument with a woman who locked herself inside a bathroom prompting Hsu to fire a round through the door before taking off in a getaway car. See also: West Palm Beach man arrested after police say he faked coma to cover up $190K embezzlement Officers with the Fort Pierce Police Department say they later located the car near Porpoise Beach, prompting a manhunt. White the search was underway, detectives and crime scene investigators continued to work the case and executed a search warrant at the Wyoming Avenue residence. Around 2:30 p.m., Hsu's family members located him and alerted a passing Fort Pierce police officer, according to investigators. Hsu was taken into custody without incident, and a firearm was recovered. Hsu was arrested and charged with Attempted Felony Murder, Kidnapping, Tampering with a Witness, Simple Battery (Domestic), and Grand Theft of a Motor Vehicle. He remains in custody without bond.

A Florida woman took a scam beyond the phone lines, showing up at a Martin County resident’s door pretending to represent a bank and demanding the victim’s credit card on Monday. According to the Martin County Sheriff’s Office , Monique Love Turnbull, of Miami, was seen at a victim’s doorstep claiming the victim’s bank account had been compromised. Turnbull asked for the victim’s credit card and said she would dispose of it. As law enforcement investigated, deputies were alerted to another call identifying Turnbull in a separate case. Body camera video shows deputies pulling Turnbull over and asking her to step out of the car. See also: Palm Beach County clerk arrested on 5 felonies involving child, suspended by DeSantis The arresting deputy then tells Turnbull she is under arrest for fraud before placing her in handcuffs. The sheriff’s office is warning residents never to allow someone into their home if the person was not scheduled to visit. Residents should also never hand over credit cards, cash, gold or other valuables to someone who shows up unexpectedly. MCSO says anyone who comes to a resident’s home claiming to represent a bank or financial institution and asking for valuables should be treated with suspicion. Residents are urged to call 911.

Incumbent Sara Baxter has won the Republican nomination for the Palm Beach County Commission District 6 seat after a contentious primary race against challenger Elizabeth Accomando.Baxter, the current county mayor, secured the victory by approximately 2,400 votes, according to the Palm Beach County Supervisor of Elections. She will now face Democratic candidate and former state House member Katherine Waldron in the November general election.WATCH WPTV'S COVERAGE BELOW:Cheers erupted at Baxter’s watch party in Wellington as the final results came in. Baxter, who was endorsed by former President Donald Trump, was emotional as she thanked her supporters."I mean, just grateful to God, grateful to my residents, grateful to the voters who saw through all the messiness these past few weeks," Baxter said. "I can't say thank you enough... and I need you to get out again and vote in November."The race was one of the most closely watched local contests, with both candidates campaigning heavily in the final days. At her watch party, challenger Elizabeth Accomando said she was proud of the grassroots campaign she ran.It's not the result she wanted but — she’s proud of her grassroots campaign, her staff and her supporters, Accomando told WPTV's Michael Hoffman. "I will still continue to be a very strong advocate for the Western communities, because I truly care about my community and all of my neighbors."Throughout election day, voters told WPTV that key issues driving them to the polls included environmental protection, managing development, the use of Flock cameras, and the potential arrival of AI data centers in the county.With the primary behind her, Baxter is now focused on the general election for the historically Republican-leaning commission seat. In her victory speech, she addressed the economic pressures facing residents.““I am incredibly grateful to the voters of District 6 and to every person who opened their door, volunteered, contributed and believed in this campaign,” said Waldron. “I have spent years serving western Palm Beach County, first on the Port Commission and then in the Florida House, and I know how much families here are being squeezed by housing costs, insurance and the everyday cost of living. In November, I will keep fighting for responsible growth, clean water, stronger infrastructure and real accountability. District 6 deserves a commissioner who shows up, asks the hard questions and owns the vote, and I am ready to make that case to every voter in this district.”.”Voters will decide between Baxter and Waldron in the general election on Nov. 5.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. Our editorial team verifies all reporting on all platforms for fairness and accuracy.

Lucie County Sheriff's Office is sounding the alarm after receiving more than 50 reports from people targeted by a scam involving callers impersonating law enforcement officers. Lucie County Sheriff's Office , scammers have been using the names of the Civil Judicial Services Bureau, Lt. Michael O'Brien and retired Sgt. Jeff Buchanan when making fraudulent calls. See also: Palm Beach County School District employee arrested by WPBPD in prostitution operation Deputies said the scam follows a repeated pattern. A caller claims the victim missed court or jury duty and that there is a warrant for their arrest. SLCSO warned that scammers may use official-sounding language and personal information to make the call appear legitimate. The sheriff's office said scammers use fear, urgency and threats of arrest to pressure victims into taking immediate action. Deputies said residents who receive one of these calls should: Hang up. Do not provide personal or financial information. Do not send money or make any payments. Do not trust the caller ID or the name provided by the caller. If you have questions about a legitimate court matter, contact the appropriate agency using a verified phone number.

hero.headline: Vero Beach homicide arrest using Flock Safety cameras sparks privacy debate in Indian River County
hero.body:
Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers credited Flock Safety license plate reader cameras with leading to an arrest in a Vero Beach homicide case after tracking a suspect to a West Virginia motel, sparking debate among residents about privacy and surveillance technology. The arrest followed what Flowers described as a cold-blooded murder in Vero Beach that triggered a multi-state manhunt. The Flock Safety system is a nationwide network of cameras connected to a searchable law enforcement database.

Flowers defended the technology's role in the investigation. "We got a murderer behind bars because of this. We got this guy off the streets because of the Flock system," Flowers said. Many residents welcomed the technology's effectiveness in the case. Larry, a Treasure Coast resident, said he thinks it is a good thing if the system can keep criminals out of residents' lives. Meghan Ford, a Treasure Coast visitor, said she sees value in using the system for serious cases like finding people who have committed horrible crimes or locating missing children.

Other community members expressed concerns about privacy as the system's use expands. "We don't have that much privacy anymore, so where do you draw the line?" Michael Maslak, a Stuart resident, said. Ford echoed the tension, saying the technology feels like an invasion of privacy for people doing the right thing in life. Recent reports indicate some officers have misused the Flock Safety system to track romantic partners, fueling controversy around the technology.

Flock Safety announced changes requiring searches to include a case number and mandating that all agencies use a new audit system designed to flag suspicious activity. Maslak said the technology is a great idea but needs to be kept under control. Treasure Coast residents say they hope regulations will continue to evolve alongside the technology's expanding uses.

hero.headline: Tornado touches down in Port St. Lucie, National Weather Service surveys damage Monday
hero.body:
The National Weather Service announced late Sunday night that it will conduct a storm survey Monday morning after a tornado touched down near Jessica Clinton Park in Port St. Lucie. The agency said a brief landspout tornado occurred in the vicinity of Jessica Clinton Park near Southbend Boulevard and SE Navy Avenue, lofting debris and producing minor damage to homes in the area.

The National Weather Service in Melbourne said the tornado likely started as a funnel cloud that touched down on the St. Lucie County side, just west of the St. Lucie River. Emergency Management officials reported several homes with minor structural damage near SE Wake Road, Navy Avenue, and West Snow Road in the Southbend area of Port St. Lucie. The tornado may have continued east toward the St. Lucie River, where it became a waterspout.

A tornado warning was issued for parts of St. Lucie and Martin counties on Sunday. Several residents submitted photos and videos of apparent funnel clouds in the sky from Port St. Lucie, Jensen Beach and Palm City. Radar data showed only a weak circulation signature at the time of the reported damage, suggesting the circulation was likely shallow and near the surface, consistent with a landspout-type event.

Aaron Christiansen, a Port St. Lucie resident who lives near Southbend Boulevard and SE Navy Avenue, said he was home around 6 p.m. Sunday when he noticed debris through his window. He took cover with his dogs in his bedroom and had about 10 seconds to react before the storm hit. His patio furniture was submerged in his pool, his pool fence was blown toward his home, and debris was scattered across his yard. Christiansen, originally from Minnesota, said his experience with tornado-like weather helped him know what precautions to take. He and his family and pets were not injured. Christiansen said he received the emergency alert after the storm had already hit and plans to begin cleanup efforts Monday and have his roof inspected.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce police identify suspect in South 14th Street homicide from July
hero.body:
Fort Pierce police identified a suspect in a deadly shooting that occurred July 5 on South 14th Street. The Fort Pierce Police Department announced that 28-year-old Cornelius Trevon Ivory was identified as the suspect in the homicide and faces charges of first-degree murder, attempted first-degree murder, possession of a firearm and possession of a firearm by a convicted felon.

The shooting happened at about 3:43 a.m. on July 5. A 28-year-old woman sustained a non-life-threatening injury to her hand, while a 28-year-old man sustained multiple gunshot wounds and was transported to a local hospital. The police department announced on July 7 that the man died from his injuries.

An initial investigation revealed that the victims were involved in an earlier altercation at the 5800 block of Okeechobee Road before returning to their residence. As the victims arrived home, a man not believed to be involved in the altercation on Okeechobee Road approached them and fired a weapon before leaving the area. Detectives developed probable cause for Ivory's arrest through an investigation that included eyewitness accounts, information from community members, law enforcement databases and assistance from the Palm Bay Police Department.

Fort Pierce Police obtained an arrest warrant charging Ivory in connection with the killing. Authorities said he was served with an arrest warrant while in the St. Lucie County Jail involving possession of weapon by a convicted felon on July 24. Ivory remains in the jail, and his first appearance in the latest case was Friday. Investigators credited members of the public who came forward with information during the case, as well as the Palm Bay Police Department for assisting in the investigation.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie man charged with five counts of sexual activity with a minor
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie police arrested a 48-year-old man Thursday morning after SWAT officers executed a search warrant at his home on Southwest Jaslo Avenue.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police arrested 48-year-old Virgil Jason Vinz without incident around 6 a.m. Thursday at a residence in the 900 block of Southwest Jaslo Avenue. The Port St. Lucie Police Department's SWAT team executed the warrant. Vinz is charged with five counts of sexual activity with a minor, a second-degree felony under Florida law, and six counts of contributing to the delinquency or dependency of a child, a first-degree misdemeanor.

The SWAT response drew attention from neighbors, several of whom reported hearing loud booms before seeing officers outside the home. Police spokesperson Brandon Martinez said the sounds were not gunshots but Noise Flash Diversionary Devices used during the SWAT team's entry into the home. Martinez said the devices are used for the safety of both officers and individuals when conducting high-risk operations.

Court records show Vinz pleaded no contest and was adjudicated guilty in 2023 on charges of battery on a law enforcement officer and contributing to the delinquency of a child. Records also show he later violated probation before completing Mental Health Court in October 2024. Jail records show Vinz remained in the St. Lucie County Jail as of Thursday night, with bond pending.

cards.headline: Disciplined St. Lucie County firefighters challenge investigation as residents call for reinstatement
cards.teaser: Three terminated St. Lucie County Fire District firefighters and community members questioned the integrity of a hazing investigation at a district meeting, calling for accountability and reinstatement.
cards.body:
Three terminated St. Lucie County Fire District firefighters and community members urged the district to reinstate the disciplined firefighters at a meeting Wednesday, alleging the investigation into hazing incidents was limited and mischaracterized. The fire district disciplined five firefighters following an independent investigation into alleged hazing incidents after videos surfaced that appeared to show the firefighters administering electric shocks to newer employees. Three firefighters were terminated.

Jordan Hutchinson, one of the terminated firefighters, said the firefighters were held accountable and that district leadership needs to be held accountable as well. The former firefighters are calling the disciplinary action retaliation for filing complaints against district leadership. Many residents at the meeting argued that the investigation produced a limited report, with some allegations reviewed internally and others by independent investigators.

A motion was made at the meeting to suspend the district chief and attorney, but the vote failed 4-1. The dispute has now moved to arbitration.

hero.headline: Multi-million dollar crane crashes off 90th Avenue in Vero Beach
hero.teaser: A six-axle crane went off the road and flipped on 90th Avenue near Oslo Road on August 19. Residents say the crash highlights road safety concerns they have been raising with the county for months.
hero.body:
Crews are working to pull a multi-million dollar, six-axle crane out of a ditch along 90th Avenue near Oslo Road in Vero Beach after it went off the road and flipped on August 19. The stretch of 90th Avenue between 4th Street and Oslo Road will be closed until the truck is removed.

Sally Rogers, who lives down the road from where the crane came to rest, said this is not the first crash she has seen on the narrow stretch of road. She said crews closed 82nd Avenue and rerouted traffic for the Oslo Road project, and drivers looking for a fast route to State Road 60 and I-95 found 90th Avenue instead. Rogers said dump trucks and semi trucks have learned this is a quick, straight shot to 60 to get on 95.

Rogers said dump trucks are not supposed to be using this route under the project's haul route plan. She also raised concerns about a bridge at 4th Street, saying she has not seen a posted weight limit and does not know whether it can handle heavier commercial traffic. Rogers said she has asked Indian River County to conduct a traffic study on the road and wants county officials to come see the road for themselves. County officials say they are looking into the matter. FDOT confirmed that this stretch of 90th Avenue is maintained by Indian River County.

For people who live nearby, the crash is the latest example of a problem they say they've been warning the county about for months. Sally Rogers lives down the road from where the crane came to rest. She said August 19th was when she first noticed the crane in the ditch. She drives this stretch of 90th Avenue constantly. "Every single day," Rogers said, when asked how often she travels the road. She said she has driven it for 11 years. Rogers said this is not the first crash she has seen on this stretch of road, which she describes as narrow. She said she does not know for certain what caused each past crash, but she believes the road itself is part of the problem. See also: 'Disgusting and shameful': Lantana mayor condemns vandalism at police memorial Rogers pointed to a recent detour as the reason commercial trucks are on this road at all. She said crews closed 82nd Avenue and rerouted traffic for the Oslo Road project , and drivers looking for a fast route to State Road 60 and I-95 found this road instead. "The dump trucks and the semi trucks have learned that this is a thruway to 60 to get on 95," Rogers said. "It's quick, it's easy, it's a straight shot." Rogers said there is no signage warning drivers the road narrows, and she said dump trucks are not supposed to be using this route at all under the project's haul route plan. She said trucks were assigned to 82nd Avenue, and only started coming this way once that road closed. Rogers also raised concerns about a bridge at 4th Street, saying she has not seen a posted weight limit and doesn't know whether it can structurally handle the heavier commercial traffic now crossing it. She described another hazard when it rains. Water pools on the low side of the road and has nowhere to drain, she said, which hides what's underneath. "You don't know if there's a hole. You don't know if there's a soft spot. You don't know if there's a washout happening," Rogers said. Rogers said the traffic has made her change her own driving habits. When she sees a truck or semi approaching on the narrower sections, she said she pulls over and waits. "I stopped on the bridge, pulled off on the side there at 4th Street and waited for the semi to come and pass, because I know it's not wide enough to comfortably pass," Rogers said. "I'd rather not." She recounted a close call involving her husband, who was driving his Dodge 3500 dually when he passed another truck pulling a trailer on the road. "The trailers actually touched," Rogers said. Rogers said she has asked Indian River County to conduct a traffic study on the road. She said the response so far has been noncommittal. "Maybe we'll do that, but I think right now we should wait," Rogers said the county told her. Her request now is simple: she wants county officials to come see the road for themselves. They need to lay eyes on it," Rogers said. Bring a county dump truck to go the opposite direction, and pass the county dump truck in the narrowest part of the road." Crews remain on scene working to remove the crashed crane. CBS12 News is asking the county if they plan on adding signage or directing trucks to go a different route. County officials say they're looking into the matter. FDOT confirmed that this stretch of 90th Ave. is maintained by Indian River County. between 4th Street and Oslo Road will be closed until the truck is removed.

hero.headline: Publix removes 10-item limit from express checkout lanes across Florida stores
hero.body:
Publix is removing the 10-item limit at its express checkout lanes across its nearly 1,500 stores in the Southern United States, including locations throughout Florida. The grocery chain said in a statement that the change is intended to improve checkout efficiency and reduce wait times at checkout.

The change is already underway at many stores and will soon expand to all Publix locations. The company made the announcement Saturday as it continues to compete in a crowded grocery market across the Southeast.

According to the American Customer Satisfaction Index, Publix ranked as the nation's No. 2 grocery store chain in 2026, behind Trader Joe's. The retailer operates stores across the Southern United States, with a significant presence in Florida where the company is headquartered.

The elimination of the item limit represents a shift in the company's checkout strategy. Express lanes have traditionally been reserved for customers with a small number of items to allow for faster transactions. Publix stated the new policy is designed to reduce overall wait times, though the company did not provide details on how removing the limit would achieve that goal or whether the lanes would retain the express designation.

cards.headline: Indian River County creates Attainable Housing Trust to support development
cards.teaser: The Indian River County Commission voted unanimously August 4 to approve a landmark Attainable Housing Trust that will operate under the guidelines of the State Housing Initiatives Partnership program and will encourage the use of surplus county-owned lands to more effectively support attainable housing developments in the county.
cards.body:
The Indian River County Commission voted unanimously August 4 to approve a landmark Attainable Housing Trust that will operate under the guidelines of the State Housing Initiatives Partnership program and will encourage the use of surplus county-owned lands to more effectively support attainable housing developments in the county. Previously on May 27, the members of the Affordable Housing Advisory Committee voted unanimously to recommend the County Commission approve the draft ordinance. County SHIP Administrator Siphi Chinyanganya provided a comprehensive review of the proposal that morning.

The Attainable Housing Trust is a separate fund from the SHIP local housing assistance program, but aligns with SHIP-based practices. It will be administered by the SHIP administrator but will maintain independent accounting and compliance. The SHIP administrator plans to seek Attainable Housing Trust funding from voluntary developer contributions, proceeds from the sale or disposition of county-owned property, grants, donations and interlocal contributions, private philanthropy donations and interest earnings on the trust fund balance itself. The Trust has safeguards including recorded affordability covenants, income limits and compliance requirements and long-term affordability protections. This will be a 50-year lien so that it remains affordable and developers will be responsible for ongoing compliance following conveyance.

Chairman Deryl Loar said the Trust is another tool for the county's toolbox. It is a trust that allows us, like other counties and municipalities, to have a mechanism in place, he said. District 2 Commissioner Joseph Flescher made a motion for approval, which Commissioner Joseph Earman seconded. The motion then passed unanimously.
cards.article_text: Chairman Deryl Loar VERO BEACH – The Indian River County Commission voted unanimously Aug. 4 to approve a landmark Attainable Housing Trust that will operate under the guidelines of the State Housing Initiatives Partnership program and will encourage the use of surplus county-owned lands to more effectively support attainable housing developments in the county. Previously on May 27, the members of the Affordable Housing Advisory Committee voted unanimously to recommend the County Commission approve the draft ordinance. County SHIP Administrator Siphi Chinyanganya provided a comprehensive review of the proposal that morning. “We’re going to explain what the Attainable Housing Trust is and we’re hoping the ordinance will be approved today,” she said. “It supports affordable and attainable housing development. The ordinance establishes the Trust focused on land acquisition, land banking and partnerships with for-profit and non-profit organizations. We’re going to look at the legal framework, the ordinance overview and the implementation process of the Trust.” Chinyanganya first pointed out the distinction between the Attainable Housing Trust and the traditional SHIP program that provides local governments funding for affordable housing. “This is a separate fund from the SHIP local housing assistance program, but it aligns with SHIP-based practices,” she explained. “It will be administered by the SHIP administrator but will maintain independent accounting and compliance. So, while the SHIP program operates under the local housing assistance plan, the trust fund would maintain separate accounting compliance and reporting requirements. The purpose of this fund is to have affordable housing recognized as a public purpose authorized under Section 125-379 of Florida Statutes, which encourages counties to identify and use surplus county-owned lands for affordable housing.” The SHIP administrator plans to seek Attainable Housing Trust funding from voluntary developer contributions, proceeds from the sale or disposition of county-owned property, grants, donations and interlocal contributions, private philanthropy donations and even interest earnings on the trust fund balance itself. She emphasized the formal county hierarchy that will oversee all facets of attainable housing development under the AHT. “At the top of the Trust will be the Board of County Commissioners [with] final authority,” she continued. “The Community Services Department will administrate the program and coordinate any events. The Affordable Housing Advisory Committee will provide an advisory role; Planning Development will review and assess properties to be acquired; and finance, county administration and the county attorney will have oversight. The SHIP administrator will develop and publish a request for qualifications to create a register of development partners. The AHAC will review the RFQ and make recommendations for eligible development partners to the BOCC, and then the BOCC will approve the eligible development partners added to the register.” As far as the disposition of properties, the Planning Development Department will first evaluate the location, zoning and infrastructural viability of each property to assess developmental feasibility. The county attorney’s office will then verify the title status and draft acquisition and conveyance language, as well as securing BOCC authorization to purchase or accept the property. Planning Development staff will subsequently classify the property as surplus and designate it for attainable housing. The SHIP administrator and Community Services staff will in turn present available properties to the AHAC. The AHAC will offer available properties to partners on the register in order of ranking. Procurement and the SHIP administrator will coordinate the property conveyance following BOCC approval. The Trust has been in safeguards for the county as well. “There will be recorded affordability covenants, income limits and compliance requirements and long-term affordability protections,” Chinyanganya explained. “This will be a 50-year lean so that it remains affordable [and] developers will be responsible for ongoing compliance following conveyance. It limits county exposure to land transactions and ensures legal and financial safeguards. We also have financial controls through a special revenue fund.” Chairman Deryl Loar offered his perspective at the conclusion of her presentation, which brought a few chuckles from the dais. “This is actually another tool for our toolbox,” he said. “It is a trust that allows us – like other counties and municipalities – to have a mechanism in place. For example, if Commissioner [Joseph] Earman, donates $100,000 for affordable housing when he retires, we will certainly accept it, put it in trust and it will be policed as we do the current SHIP program.” When no members of the public came forward to comment afterward, District 2 Commissioner Joseph Flescher made a motion for approval. “Commissioner Earman just said that I was retiring beforehand, so I want to set up my commitment as well and we’ll take a look at that,” he said as laughter again broke out in the Chambers. “Motion to approve.” Commissioner Earman seconded that motion, which then passed unanimously. cards.teaser: The Humane Society of Vero Beach and Indian River County teams up with NBCUniversal Local for the annual Clear the Shelters special adoption event Saturday, August 22, from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.
cards.body:

We have so many wonderful dogs and cats that deserve homes, and Clear the Shelters is the perfect way for families to discover them, said Nichola Redmond, HSVB Chief Executive Officer. This year, Hills Pet Nutrition joins as a presenting sponsor, providing adoption kits at select shelters that include starter bags of Hills Science Diet food, coupons and other helpful supplies for new pet families.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce police identify suspect in July 5 homicide on South 14th Street
hero.body:
Fort Pierce police have identified 28-year-old Cornelius Trevon Ivory as the suspect in a July 5 homicide on South 14th Street and charged him with first-degree murder. The shooting occurred at approximately 3:43 a.m. when a man approached two victims at their residence and fired a weapon before leaving the area. A 28-year-old woman sustained a non-life-threatening injury to her hand, while a 28-year-old man suffered multiple gunshot wounds and was transported to a local hospital, where he died from his injuries on July 7.

Investigators determined the victims had been involved in an earlier altercation at the 5800 block of Okeechobee Road before returning to their residence. The shooter was not believed to be involved in the altercation on Okeechobee Road. Detectives developed probable cause for Ivory's arrest through an extensive investigation that included eyewitness accounts, information from community members, law enforcement databases, and assistance from the Palm Bay Police Department.

Ivory faces charges of first-degree murder, attempted first-degree murder, possession of a firearm, and possession of a firearm by a convicted felon. He was served with the arrest warrant while in the St. Lucie County Jail on July 24, where he was being held on unrelated charges involving possession of a weapon by a convicted felon. His first appearance in the homicide case was Friday.

Ivory remains in the St. Lucie County Jail. Investigators credited members of the public who came forward with information during the case. The investigation remains active, and anyone with additional information is encouraged to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department.

cards.headline: Terminated St. Lucie County firefighters challenge hazing investigation at district meeting
cards.teaser: Three fired St. Lucie County firefighters questioned the integrity of a hazing investigation at a district meeting Wednesday, calling the disciplinary action retaliation for filing complaints against leadership.
cards.body:
Three terminated St. Lucie County firefighters challenged the investigation that led to their firing at a St. Lucie County Fire District meeting Wednesday, alleging the probe into hazing incidents was limited and mischaracterized. The fire district disciplined five firefighters following an independent investigation into alleged hazing incidents after videos surfaced that appeared to show the firefighters administering electric shocks to newer employees. Three firefighters were terminated.

Jordan Hutchinson, one of the terminated firefighters, said at the meeting that the disciplinary action was retaliation for filing complaints against district leadership. Many residents argued that the investigation produced a limited report, with some allegations reviewed internally and others by independent investigators. Community members urged the district to reinstate the disciplined firefighters.

A motion was made at the meeting to suspend the district chief and attorney, but the vote failed 4-1. The dispute has now moved to arbitration.

hero.headline: Martin County deputy stops $600,000 gold bar scam targeting senior
hero.teaser: A Martin County senior nearly lost his life savings of $600,000 to a gold bar scam before a sheriff's deputy intervened and stopped the transaction.
hero.body:
A Martin County senior nearly lost $600,000 in a gold bar scam, but was able to get his money returned through the efforts of a Martin County Sheriff's Office deputy. The victim was told by someone claiming to represent the victim's financial institution that the victim's bank account was compromised and the safest way to protect his money was to back it up with gold. The victim was instructed to send $600,000, his life savings, to a legitimate gold vendor, where the gold would then be picked up by a third party driver and supposedly be delivered to the bank, according to a sheriff's office Facebook posting.

hero.headline: St. Lucie Mets fall 6-3 to Lakeland Flying Tigers at Clover Park
hero.body:
The Lakeland Flying Tigers defeated the St. Lucie Mets 6-3 on Friday night at Clover Park in Port St. Lucie. The loss extended the Mets' losing streak to seven consecutive games and marked their 11th loss in the last 12 games. Lakeland scored the first four runs of the game before the Mets mounted a late rally.

Yovanny Rodriguez hit a solo home run to lead off the bottom of the seventh inning to cut the Mets deficit to 4-2. Aiden Robbins homered in the eighth inning off Jose Guzman to make it 4-3. Eli Serrano III followed with a double and advanced to third base on a fly out, but Guzman struck out Rodriguez looking to end the inning and strand Serrano III on third. The first two batters of the top of the ninth drew walks against Jonathan Jimenez and Miguel Mejias, and both runners scored on a ground ball error and sacrifice fly to extend the Lakeland lead to 6-3.

Dylan Carey went 3 for 4 with three singles in the loss. Bohan Adderley went 2 for 4 with a double. The Mets used seven pitchers. Starter Camden Lohman pitched a scoreless first inning. Nate Isler, the Mets 10th round draft pick out of Dartmouth, pitched the second inning and gave up three runs in his professional debut, surrendering a home run to Jude Warwick. Mets 14th round pick Zach Crotchfelt out of Troy made his professional debut in the third inning and retired the side in order with a strikeout. Jimenez pitched the longest outing, going 3.0 innings and being charged with one earned run.

Lakeland reliever Xiomer Guacache pitched 3.1 innings after a 1 hour and 18 minute rain delay to get the win. He allowed two runs on four hits. Lakeland starter Malachi Witherspoon struck out five in 3.0 scoreless innings. Guzman pitched the final two innings and was credited with his fifth save. The Mets now stand at 17-34 in the second half and 50-67 overall, while the Flying Tigers improved to 26-24 and 57-58. The teams play the fifth game of their series at Clover Park on Saturday, when the Mets will wear special jerseys to celebrate the 100th anniversary of St. Anastasias School in Fort Pierce. A postgame fireworks show is scheduled.

hero.headline: Field of Greens to open first Treasure Coast location in Port St. Lucie
hero.body:
Field of Greens will open its first Treasure Coast location Aug. 29 at 10400 SW Discovery Way in Port St. Lucie, serving salads, smoothies, wraps, bowls and plant-forward meals for breakfast and lunch. The Florida-based chain specializes in fresh, nutrient-rich dishes and scratch cooking.

The new location marks a milestone for the company. Founded in West Palm Beach in 2003, this will be the tenth Field of Greens location. Port St. Lucie is the company's first venture outside of Palm Beach County, according to Dan Morris, Field of Greens vice president. Morris said the community is seeing tremendous growth and represents an opportunity to bring the restaurant's fresh, healthy offerings to new audiences.

The menu includes soups, sandwiches, wraps, bowls, vegan options and cold-pressed juices. Prices at the North Palm Beach location range from $5 for a cup of soup to $14 for the Full of Life Salad, made with arugula, spinach, roasted chicken, quinoa, craisins, almonds, cherry tomato, mint, feta and basil honey. The restaurant also offers a children's menu and desserts.

Field of Greens plans to open additional locations next year in the Martin Downs Village Center plaza in Palm City, Avenir in Palm Beach Gardens and President Donald J. Trump International Airport. The Port St. Lucie location offers both counter service and takeout from 9 a.m. to close.

hero.headline: Vero Beach man arrested on attempted murder charge after birthday party assault
hero.body:
Collin Ryan Smith, 25, of the 4900 block of Corsica Square in Vero Beach, was arrested on July 17 on charges including attempted murder after a birthday party ended and no one would take him to a local bar. Indian River County Sheriff's deputies responded to a home in the 2400 block of 86th Drive in Vero Beach at about 1:49 a.m. on July 17 for a disturbance in progress.

Four people told deputies that Smith wanted someone to take him to a local bar as the party settled down. When no one offered, he started yelling and waking up people in the house. One woman told Smith to leave but he grabbed her hair and dragged her down a hallway into a kitchen where he got on top of her and began choking her until she was unconscious. Another woman told officers that when she came out of her room, Smith grabbed her by the hair, pulled her outside and threw her to the ground. A third woman said she saw Smith throw a woman into a ditch outside the house and when she tried to stop him, he hit her in the mouth and threw her to the ground. Smith then pressed her against the side of a car and pressed her neck, causing a restriction of blood flow to her head.

A man at the house intervened by fighting Smith off the three women. A neighbor said when he heard screaming, he went outside and saw Smith pick a woman up and slam her to the ground. Deputies found a bullet in one woman's bedroom, which she said fell out of Smith's pocket. Smith then left in a Ford pickup truck and was subsequently stopped in the 1400 block of 96 Street in Vero Beach.

Smith was booked into the Indian River County Jail on July 17 at 3:49 a.m. He was in the Indian River County Jail as of July 21 on no bond for possession of a weapon or ammunition by a convicted felon. He also faces $150,000 bond for attempted murder, $50,000 bond for two counts of battery by strangulation, $25,000 bond for aggravated battery, $5,000 bond for criminal mischief, and $5,000 bond each for DUI, driving while license suspended, refusal to submit to a DUI test, and possession of drug paraphernalia. Officers said Smith smelled of alcohol and refused to take a breathalyzer test. A glass smoking device was found in his pocket.

cards.headline: Flock license plate readers helped track Vero Beach homicide suspect from Orlando to West Virginia, sheriff says
cards.teaser: A Sebastian man accused of fatally shooting a Vero Beach hairdresser was arrested Wednesday night by U.S. Marshals at a West Virginia motel. Sheriff Eric Flowers credited the department's license plate reader technology as critical to the rapid arrest.
cards.body:
Matthew Allen Waggle, 33, faces a first-degree murder charge in the death of Dawn Kriskewic, 52, according to the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. Detectives are working to extradite Waggle from West Virginia to face charges locally. Deputies responded to a 911 call at approximately 8:41 a.m. Sunday reporting a woman in the roadway in the 500 block of 1st Street in Vero Beach. First responders found Kriskewic suffering from an apparent gunshot wound and immediately began life-saving measures. Kriskewic was transported to a trauma center where she was later pronounced dead.

Sheriff Eric Flowers said during a Thursday news conference that Waggle and Kriskewic were in an on-and-off relationship, and that the victim had recently ended things with the suspect. According to investigators, Waggle traveled by Greyhound bus from an unknown location to the Orlando area, then took an Uber ride directly to Kriskewic's Vero Beach home Sunday morning. Security footage captured Waggle walking to the residence, having a brief interaction with Kriskewic, shooting her and then leaving the scene. The sheriff said Waggle was at the location for approximately 10 to 15 minutes before fleeing the area after the shooting.

After the shooting, Waggle took another Uber back to Orlando, boarded a Greyhound bus to North Carolina, and ultimately traveled to a motel near Dunbar, West Virginia. Detectives determined that Waggle's ex-wife was making calls to a specific West Virginia motel, which helped lead authorities to his location. Marshals arrested Waggle at the motel Wednesday night. Flowers credited the department's license plate reader technology, including the Flock system, as critical to the rapid arrest. I'm not standing here four days later telling you about this guy being in custody in West Virginia, Flowers said. So, for everybody who wants to talk about how bad this system is, we got a murderer behind bars because of this.
cards.article_text: A Sebastian man accused of fatally shooting a Vero Beach hairdresser was arrested Wednesday night by U.S. Marshals at a West Virginia motel, ending a multi-state manhunt that began after the domestic violence homicide Sunday morning in Indian River County. Matthew Allen Waggle, 33, faces a first-degree murder charge in the death of Dawn Kriskewic, 52, according to the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office. Detectives are working to extradite Waggle from West Virginia to face charges locally. Deputies responded to a 911 call at approximately 8:41 a.m. Sunday reporting a woman in the roadway in the 500 block of 1st Street in Vero Beach. First responders found Kriskewic suffering from an apparent gunshot wound and immediately began life-saving measures, according to the sheriff’s office. Kriskewic was transported to a trauma center where she was later pronounced dead. Investigators classified her death as a domestic violence homicide. Sheriff Eric Flowers said during a Thursday news conference that Waggle and Kriskewic were in an on-and-off relationship, and that the victim had recently ended things with the suspect. “She had actually told her co-workers, ‘If he calls, if he shows up, I want nothing to do with him. Tell him, I’m not here,’” Flowers said. “She had broken things off with him, he had moved away and somehow she knew that he could potentially be coming to the area.” According to investigators, Waggle traveled by Greyhound bus from an unknown location to the Orlando area, then took an Uber ride directly to Kriskewic’s Vero Beach home Sunday morning. “You see that video of him walking, he was dropped off around the corner, he made his way in, we’ve got him on video, on Ring doorbells, on a variety of different security cameras,” Flowers said. The sheriff said Waggle was at the location for approximately 10 to 15 minutes before fleeing the area after the shooting. Security footage captured Waggle walking to the residence, having a brief interaction with Kriskewic, shooting her and then leaving the scene. After the shooting, Waggle took another Uber back to Orlando, boarded a Greyhound bus to North Carolina, and ultimately traveled to a motel near Dunbar, West Virginia, according to investigators. The sheriff’s office real-time crime center played a crucial role in tracking Waggle’s movements across state lines. Detectives determined that Waggle’s ex-wife was making calls to a specific West Virginia motel, which helped lead authorities to his location. Marshals arrested Waggle at the motel Wednesday night. His ex-wife was also taken into custody at the scene and is cooperating with investigators. “At this moment, we don’t have charges on her, but we are actively speaking with her,” Flowers said. Investigators said Waggle left the firearm used in the shooting and other evidence near the scene in Vero Beach. The gun was later determined to belong to Waggle’s ex-wife, according to the sheriff’s office. Flowers credited the department’s license plate reader technology, including the Flock system, as critical to the rapid arrest. “I’m not standing here four days later telling you about this guy being in custody in West Virginia,” Flowers said. “So, for everybody who wants to talk about how bad this system is, we got a murderer behind bars because of this.” The investigation moved from discovering Kriskewic’s body Sunday morning to making an arrest in West Virginia by Wednesday night — a timeline Flowers called “unbelievable police work.” Two Indian River County detectives were in West Virginia interviewing Waggle and his ex-wife at the time of Thursday’s announcement. Waggle will be extradited back to Indian River County to face the first-degree murder charge. cards.headline: Body camera video shows U.S. Marshals arrest Vero Beach murder suspect in West Virginia
cards.body:
The Indian River County Sheriff's Office released body camera footage showing U.S. Marshals arresting Matthew Waggle, wanted for the murder of his ex-girlfriend Dawn Kriskewic in Vero Beach, at a motel in West Virginia on Wednesday night. Kriskewic was shot to death in front of her home on First Street in Vero Beach last Sunday. The video captures officers shouting commands during the arrest, including "Get the (expletive) down!" and "Give me your hands!" as they placed Waggle in handcuffs.

Sheriff Eric Flowers said Kriskewic had told co-workers at her hair salon that if Waggle called or showed up, she wanted nothing to do with him and instructed them to tell him she was not there. "He murdered her in cold blood in the street," Flowers said. Investigators believe Waggle traveled to Vero Beach from Orlando using an Uber, stayed just long enough to kill Kriskewic, and then left town in another Uber.

Flowers explained at a news conference Thursday how investigators tracked Waggle to the West Virginia motel where he was arrested. Waggle currently remains in jail in West Virginia.

Authorities in Florida are working on extraditing Waggle back to Indian River County to face charges. The sheriff credited the department's Real Time Crime Center and Flock license plate cameras with helping locate Waggle.

hero.headline: Fired St. Lucie County firefighters challenge hazing investigation at district meeting
hero.body:
Three firefighters terminated by St. Lucie County Fire District following an investigation into alleged hazing incidents appeared at a district meeting Wednesday to challenge the integrity of the investigation and call for their reinstatement. The firefighters were among five disciplined after an independent investigation into incidents that included videos appearing to show firefighters administering electric shocks to newer employees.

Jordan Hutchinson, one of the terminated firefighters, told the district board that the investigation was limited and mischaracterized. He and other former firefighters are calling the disciplinary action retaliation for filing complaints against district leadership. Community members urged the district to reinstate the firefighters at the meeting.

Many residents at the Wednesday meeting argued that the investigation produced a limited report, with some allegations reviewed internally and others by independent investigators. One resident asked the board to bring the firefighters home. A motion was made at the meeting to suspend the district chief and attorney, but the vote failed 4-1.

The dispute has now moved to arbitration. Hutchinson said the firefighters were held accountable and that district leadership needs to be held accountable as well.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County residents call for reinstatement of three fired firefighters at board meeting
cards.teaser: Nearly every public speaker at Wednesday's St. Lucie County Fire District Board meeting urged leaders to reinstate three firefighters terminated following a hazing investigation.
cards.body:
A St. Lucie County Fire District Board meeting Wednesday turned into a show of support for three firefighters who were fired following an investigation into hazing allegations, with nearly every public speaker urging district leaders to reinstate them. The packed meeting lasted about three hours. While board members spent part of the meeting discussing the district's upcoming budget, much of the public comment period focused on criticism of Fire Chief Jeff Lee and the controversy surrounding the firefighters' terminations.

Two of the terminated firefighters, Jordon Hutchinson and Christopher Baldwin, addressed the board publicly for the first time since their firings. Both questioned the integrity of the investigation that led to the disciplinary action. The former firefighters alleged district leadership retaliated against them after they raised concerns with the Board of Commissioners and filed internal grievances months before they were fired. Fire Chief Jeff Lee said he has been trying for weeks to reinstate the terminated firefighters but is currently unable to do so.

The St. Lucie County Fire District fired the three senior firefighters and suspended two others last month over hazing allegations after videos surfaced showing rookie firefighters being shocked with a modified bug zapper. During the meeting, a motion was made to suspend both Fire Chief Lee and the district's attorney, but the motion failed. The dispute is now in arbitration. Fire Board Chair and Port St. Lucie Mayor Shannon Martin was absent from Wednesday's meeting.
cards.article_text: Lucie County Fire District Board meeting turned into a show of support for three firefighters who were fired following an investigation into hazing allegations, with nearly every public speaker urging district leaders to reinstate them. The packed meeting lasted about three hours Wednesday. While board members spent part of the meeting discussing the district's upcoming budget, much of the public comment period focused on criticism of Fire Chief Jeff Lee and the controversy surrounding the firefighters' terminations. Several speakers called on the board to bring the terminated firefighters back. "I'm asking you respectfully to bring these firefighters home," one speaker told the board. Others questioned the district's handling of the investigation. "I think you've made a mockery of these three men," another speaker said. "It seems like you retaliated against these guys." See also: Deputies arrest man, 27, accused of traveling to meet 14-year-old in Hallandale Beach Another commenter said to the chief, "I don't know how you sleep at night." Last month, the St. Lucie County Fire District fired three senior firefighters and suspended two others over hazing allegations after videos surfaced showing rookie firefighters being shocked with a modified bug zapper. Two of the terminated firefighters, Jordon Hutchinson and Christopher Baldwin, addressed the board publicly for the first time since their firings. Both questioned the integrity of the investigation that led to the disciplinary action. "We were held accountable. They need to be held accountable," Hutchinson said. The former firefighters alleged district leadership retaliated against them after they raised concerns with the Board of Commissioners and filed internal grievances months before they were fired. "There is absolutely a culture problem, and ultimately we were trying to address a problem, and in doing so this is what's happened to us," Baldwin said. Fire Chief Jeff Lee also addressed the crowd, saying he has been trying for weeks to reinstate the terminated firefighters but is currently unable to do so. "For anybody to assume, or make assumption that I don't care about the people of this fire district, they're wrong," Lee said. Lee also acknowledged that the district does not currently have a formal process for handling internal complaints involving the fire chief. "I can't fix that problem. The board has to fix that problem," Lee said. Hutchinson and Baldwin said they want their jobs back but are not willing to withdraw their complaints against the fire district and the chief. "All we've been trying to do is make sure nobody else in this fire department ends up where we are right now," Hutchinson said. "We've been trying to fix the process the entire time, and even after being fired, we're still here today trying to fix the process." The dispute is now in arbitration. During the meeting, a motion was also made to suspend both Fire Chief Lee and the district's attorney, but the motion failed. Fire Board Chair and Port St. Lucie Mayor Shannon Martin was absent from Wednesday's meeting . Board members did not provide a reason for her absence. CBS12 reached out to Martin for comment but had not received a response.

cards.headline: Off-duty St. Lucie County deputy spots burglary suspect, leads to arrest near Port St. Lucie
cards.body:
An off-duty St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office deputy spotted and helped capture a suspected burglar Friday in the Spanish Lakes One community near Port St. Lucie. Herman Nettles, 44, was taken into custody on U.S. 1 after the deputy recognized him from an internal alert about burglaries in the 55-plus community.

Deputy Martinez-Delgado had been assigned to investigate the burglaries and attempted car burglaries earlier this week. Information about the case, including a photo of Nettles and a map showing the location of eight reported incidents, was shared with sheriff's office personnel. Two days later, the off-duty deputy noticed Nettles while she was driving and alerted responding deputies.

Nettles is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail on a charge of burglary of an unoccupied conveyance unarmed. Following the investigation, he will face a total of eight charges, including five counts of attempted burglary of an unoccupied conveyance unarmed and three counts of burglary of an unoccupied conveyance unarmed.

Sheriff Richard Del Toro said Deputy Martinez-Delgado's quick recognition and immediate action helped bring the suspect into custody. Robert Quinn, a Spanish Lakes resident, praised the deputy's attention to duty while off the clock.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce police identify suspect in deadly shooting day after Fourth of July
hero.body:
Fort Pierce Police Department identified Cornelius Trevon Ivory as the suspect in a shooting on South 14th Street that killed a 28-year-old man the day after the Fourth of July. Investigators obtained a warrant charging Ivory in connection with the shooting. Ivory was served with the warrant while in custody at the St. Lucie County Jail, where he is being held on unrelated charges.

The shooting occurred at about 3:43 a.m. on South 14th Street. When officers arrived, they found two victims suffering from gunshot wounds. A woman had been shot in the hand, while a 28-year-old man suffered multiple gunshot wounds.

The 28-year-old man was taken to a hospital, where he later died. Police announced the identification of Ivory as the suspect on Friday.

Ivory faces charges in connection with the shooting. He remains in the St. Lucie County Jail on both the new charges and the unrelated charges for which he was already in custody.

hero.headline: Florida TaxWatch releases county-by-county analysis of Amendment 3 property tax proposal
hero.body:
Florida TaxWatch launched an online resource center Friday to help voters understand Amendment 3, a property tax measure on the November ballot that would cut local property tax revenue by an estimated $45.8 billion over five years. The Florida Property Tax Resource Center includes an interactive county map, local millage rates, frequently asked questions and estimates showing potential revenue losses for local governments across the state.

Amendment 3 would expand Florida's homestead exemption for non-school property taxes to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028. School property taxes would remain unchanged. The proposal would also reduce the annual assessment-growth cap on non-homestead properties, including rental homes, second homes and commercial properties, from 10% to 5%. The measure must receive at least 60% support from voters to become part of the Florida Constitution.

Florida TaxWatch has not yet taken an official position on the amendment. President and CEO Jeff Kottkamp said the organization will announce its recommendation in a broader constitutional amendment guide expected next month. The new resource center does not include a calculator showing how much individual homeowners could save because cities and counties could respond to the revenue loss by cutting services, increasing millage rates or imposing new fees and special assessments, according to TaxWatch.

Opponents of the amendment argue the proposal would shift costs rather than eliminate them, potentially forcing communities to reduce spending on police, firefighters, emergency medical services, libraries and other local programs. Jackson Peel with Save Our Services said Amendment 3 is a scam and a tax shift that will either raise costs or take away services Floridians rely on. The ballot summary was recently rewritten after a Leon County judge found the Legislature's original wording biased and misleading. A private calculator created by Casey Vockell of My Exemption Check found that a Hillsborough County home assessed at $500,000 could save less than $209 per month by 2028, though the estimate does not account for any later decisions by local governments.

School property taxes would remain unchanged.The proposal would also reduce the annual assessment-growth cap on non-homestead properties from 10% to 5%. hero.headline: Vero Beach Table Tennis Club faces closure as owner seeks community support
hero.teaser: The Vero Beach Table Tennis Club is on the verge of closing due to unpaid rent and utilities combined with financial difficulties from the pandemic.
hero.body:
Tyson McCoy, owner of the Vero Beach Table Tennis Club, said the club is facing closure due to unpaid rent and utilities, combined with financial difficulties during the pandemic. "The first four years here, it's been a rough battle," McCoy said. McCoy said he worries about what closure would mean for his members and others who rely on the club.

Member Daniel Freedman has been coming to the club for three years and said keeping it open is a priority. "We have to do whatever we can to make sure that this club stays open," Freedman said. Fellow member Cielo Galman said the club has built something rare. "Table tennis has a very strong social culture," Galman said. "They're like a second family to me."

McCoy created a GoFundMe to help support the club. The community has already donated $2,400. "I'm not much of a crier, but it definitely brings a tear to my eye that we have so many supporters that feel about this club the way that I do," McCoy said.

cards.headline: Multi-million dollar crane crashes off 90th Avenue in Vero Beach as residents raise traffic concerns
cards.teaser: Crews are working to pull a six-axle crane out of a ditch along 90th Avenue near Oslo Road in Vero Beach after it went off the road and flipped on August 19.
cards.body:
Crews are still working to pull a multi-million dollar, six-axle crane out of a ditch along 90th Avenue near Oslo Road in Vero Beach, after it went off the road and flipped on August 19. For people who live nearby, the crash is the latest example of a problem they say they've been warning the county about for months. Sally Rogers lives down the road from where the crane came to rest and said she has driven this stretch of 90th Avenue constantly for 11 years.

Rogers said this is not the first crash she has seen on this stretch of road, which she describes as narrow. She pointed to a recent detour as the reason commercial trucks are on this road at all. She said crews closed 82nd Avenue and rerouted traffic for the Oslo Road project, and drivers looking for a fast route to State Road 60 and I-95 found this road instead. "The dump trucks and the semi trucks have learned that this is a thruway to 60 to get on 95," Rogers said. "It's quick, it's easy, it's a straight shot."

Rogers said there is no signage warning drivers the road narrows, and she said dump trucks are not supposed to be using this route at all under the project's haul route plan. She said she has asked Indian River County to conduct a traffic study on the road. County officials say they're looking into the matter. FDOT confirmed that this stretch of 90th Avenue between 4th Street and Oslo Road is maintained by Indian River County and will be closed until the truck is removed.

She said she has driven it for 11 years. Rogers said this is not the first crash she has seen on this stretch of road, which she describes as narrow. She said she does not know for certain what caused each past crash, but she believes the road itself is part of the problem. She said crews closed 82nd Avenue and rerouted traffic for the Oslo Road project , and drivers looking for a fast route to State Road 60 and I-95 found this road instead. "The dump trucks and the semi trucks have learned that this is a thruway to 60 to get on 95," Rogers said. "It's quick, it's easy, it's a straight shot." Rogers said there is no signage warning drivers the road narrows, and she said dump trucks are not supposed to be using this route at all under the project's haul route plan. She said trucks were assigned to 82nd Avenue, and only started coming this way once that road closed. Rogers also raised concerns about a bridge at 4th Street, saying she has not seen a posted weight limit and doesn't know whether it can structurally handle the heavier commercial traffic now crossing it. She described another hazard when it rains. Water pools on the low side of the road and has nowhere to drain, she said, which hides what's underneath. "You don't know if there's a hole. You don't know if there's a soft spot. You don't know if there's a washout happening," Rogers said. Rogers said the traffic has made her change her own driving habits. When she sees a truck or semi approaching on the narrower sections, she said she pulls over and waits. "I stopped on the bridge, pulled off on the side there at 4th Street and waited for the semi to come and pass, because I know it's not wide enough to comfortably pass," Rogers said. "I'd rather not." She recounted a close call involving her husband, who was driving his Dodge 3500 dually when he passed another truck pulling a trailer on the road. "The trailers actually touched," Rogers said. Rogers said she has asked Indian River County to conduct a traffic study on the road. She said the response so far has been noncommittal. "Maybe we'll do that, but I think right now we should wait," Rogers said the county told her. Her request now is simple: she wants county officials to come see the road for themselves. They need to lay eyes on it," Rogers said. Bring a county dump truck to go the opposite direction, and pass the county dump truck in the narrowest part of the road." hero.headline: Florida Tax Watch launches online tool showing county-by-county impact of Amendment 3 property tax measure
hero.body:
Florida Tax Watch has launched a Property Tax Resource Center that allows voters to see how Amendment 3 would affect property taxes in each of Florida's counties and municipalities before the November election. The online tool provides a breakdown of the proposed property tax measure's projected five-year impact across the state.

Amendment 3 would expand the homestead exemption to $250,000 by 2028, which could reduce local property taxes by nearly $46 billion over five years statewide. The amendment requires 60% voter approval to pass. The Florida Tax Watch website features a state map where users can highlight any county to view projected impacts for each fiscal year. The tool also allows users to click through to see the impact on individual municipalities within each county.

Each county receives rankings in different categories through the tool. St. Lucie County ranks first in the state for millage and 16th in per capita property tax levies. The online resource includes data for counties across Florida, including Palm Beach, St. Lucie, Martin, Indian River and Okeechobee.

Palm Beach County plans to launch its own online tool in September where homeowners can calculate the direct impact the amendment would have on their individual property taxes. Palm Beach County Property Appraiser Dorothy Jacks said the tool will give taxpayers a clear, personal picture of what a yes vote would mean for them. Jacks said she wants to convey to taxpayers the exact number they would continue to pay in addition to what they would save on the homestead exemption increase. Several other Florida counties have similar online tools available.
